messages:
Alex R.: Heads-up — I pushed an initial RFC draft for customer-managed network integration. Sharing the proposed connectivity contract and acceptance checklist in this thread.
Marta L.: Thanks Alex. Quick clarifying Qs: who is expected to own eBGP sessions vs static routes? The customer brief said they want to manage ASN and the BGP session.
Alex R.: Correct — customer will terminate BGP on their edge. Our edge accepts learned prefixes. We plan to do next-hop rewrite for internal routing and apply per-customer route policies.
Cheng W.: Need to confirm CIDR handoff: customer will provide a public /22 for egress and an internal /16 tenancy, or do they want to advertise multiple prefixes?
Sami K.: For scope: we should support both NAT egress + direct SNAT-free routing. Acceptance should include a 72h pilot with synthetic traffic to validate stability and cost cones.
RJ (sec): Security items to add: flow logs enabled for the peering VPC, KMS-protected keys for any key material, and a default-deny L3 ACL template. Also require prefix filters on our side.
Alex R.: Draft acceptance checklist (rough):
  1) BGP session established and routes learned in <60s after neighbor up.
  2) Advertised prefixes receive inbound traffic and reach model nodes.
  3) No cross-tenant leakage to other Redwood VPCs.
  4) Automated monitoring triggers on route withdrawals/flaps (pager within 5m).
  5) Security appendix validated by RJ.
Marta L.: Add deterministic fallback: if customer withdraws prefixes, traffic should failover to regional fallback model within 30s. Add that as a gating criterion.
Cheng W.: Operational runbook request: include exact debug commands and sample outputs (e.g., `show ip bgp neighbors`, `tcpdump` snippets). We need that for solutions onboarding.
Sami K.: Rollout plan suggestion: pilot with one internal dev cluster, then pilot customer A for 48h canary, then expand to customer B before GA. Document rollback steps.
Alex R.: Config snippet for onboarding (to include in RFC):
```
neighbors:
  - asn: 64512
    ip: 203.0.113.5
    hold_time: 90
    max_prefix: 500
advertised_prefixes:
  - 198.51.100.0/22
maintenance_window: "2026-04-12T02:00:00Z"
```
RJ (sec): Also enforce max-prefix and prefix-filtering on our edge. Deny any more-specific than /24 unless preapproved.
Marta L.: Question on IPAM: do we require customers to provide a CSV mapping for advertised prefixes -> logical tenant name? That will change the onboarding automation effort.
Cheng W.: Prefer: customer uploads CSV, we run a validator (checks overlap, RFC1918 rules, prefix lengths), then schedule a maintenance window once validated. Include validator sample error messages in RFC.
Alex R.: Prioritization note: this is customer-driven but medium company-wide priority. Need sign-off from Security (RJ) and Solutions (Sami) before we commit infra time.
Sami K.: I'll assemble the pilot runbook and a step-by-step validation checklist for Solutions. Can we aim to kick off the pilot next Tuesday?
Alex R.: Works for me. @Marta L. @RJ (sec) can you confirm feasibility by EOD Monday? If yes I'll lock calendar and open the pilot tickets. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: RFC created: /rfc/customer-vpc-onprem-integration-draft.md
Cheng W.: Linked ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/ENG-1523
Marta L.: Noted — will review security appendix and post inline comments by Monday EOD.
